Jordan / team / Diego (cc),

Quick legal note and proposed language for FinOptima's request. I ran this against our standing DPA (section numbers reference the current template):

- Notification timeline: our DPA defines "discovery" as the earliest internal alert of potential unauthorized access. We can provide an initial technical notice within 72 hours of confirmed discovery; preliminary triage notes can be shared earlier if mutually agreed in writing.
- Scope of notice: we can provide a technical summary (root cause analysis, affected categories, estimated record counts) and, upon documented request, a forensic export. For full forensic exports we require evidence export approval form + a signed export agreement that includes use restrictions and chain-of-custody acknowledgement.
- Subprocessor disclosure: we are prepared to provide the roster of subprocessors that processed the affected data. We cannot temporarily move data off a third-party subprocessor and guarantee immediate suspension unless the subprocessor agrees; for managed subprocessors we can request a pause and target 24–48 hour execution.
- Escrow / custody: we generally do not place forensic images in third-party escrow by default. If FinOptima requires escrow we will need: (a) written justification, (b) a limited-scope escrow agreement, and (c) explicit permitted uses.

Draft language (for your review):
"Redwood shall notify Customer of any confirmed security incident affecting Customer Data within seventy-two (72) hours of confirmation. Redwood shall provide an initial technical summary and, upon Customer request and execution of an export authorization form, provide a forensic export and custody attestation. Redwood will disclose the subprocessors that processed the affected Customer Data; Redwood will request temporary suspension of subprocessor processing where feasible and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain such suspension within forty-eight (48) hours of a valid request."

Marissa — please build an operational checklist that maps each contractual commitment above to an owner and ETA. Ben — flag any commercial impact (credits/SLA exceptions) if we make exceptions.

Kimberly Park
